steps.purpose: Remove empty and failing samples (MAD rule, per slide) and near-empty features before normalising.
Split every count into a half that finds groups and a half that tests them, so markers are not tested on the data that defined the groups.
Normalise depth on the fit half (log or Pearson residuals, chosen by remaining depth signal) and keep variable features chosen within each slide.
Reduce the normalised features to the principal components that exceed their permutation null.
Measure how strongly slides separate the samples, within each patient, and how batches coincide with 'label' (report only).
A count VAE conditioned on slide as a non-linear correction candidate next to Harmony and ComBat.
Compare Harmony, ComBat, the count VAE and no correction for slide effects; keep the best mixing that preserves within-slide neighbourhoods (label-free; label silhouette reported only).
Screen pretrained encoders on patient-held-out pairs and extract histology image features, with stain normalisation decided from the measured colour differences.
Find spatial domains: features joined with their neighbourhood mean (BANKSY-style), number of domains chosen by subsample stability and spatial coherence.
Compare the discovered domains with the histological annotation 'label' (validation only: never used to choose).
Depth-normalise all QC-passed counts, keeping essentially every detected feature, so spatial-variability tests are not driven by spatially varying library size.
Find spatially variable features (Moran's I within slides, BH FDR, permutation calibration) on depth-normalised counts; the test does not use the discovered groups.
Test which domains border each other more or less often than chance (label permutations within slides).
How well histology image features alone predict the discovered domains under patient-grouped cross-validation; the expression arm is a ceiling reference only.
Marker genes per domain: patient pseudobulk, paired moderated t-test, BH FDR, on the held-out half of the counts; the naive per-sample test is reported for comparison.
A two-dimensional map of the corrected representation for the report, method chosen by trustworthiness and stability.

The objective asks to discover groups and to test markers between them; count splitting (data thinning) makes the two independent.

decisions.chosen: across all slides (also removing patient differences)
decisions.rationale: Markers are tested with the patient as the replicate, so discovered groups must recur across patients; patient differences dominate the data (high in the register) and a correction inside each patient would keep them, leaving groups confined to single patients. Slide effects within patients are still measured by the batch assessment.
Samples are nested in patients (8 levels); the independent unit is the coarsest grouping.

decisions.rationale: Each relevant challenge is matched to the steps whose tool addresses its type and whose inputs derive from its data; every high-severity one (6) must be handled or accepted.

decisions.chosen: add norm_all (normalize_counts on @qc.counts, n_features 10000, batch-aware) and run spatial_svg on its output instead of raw counts
decisions.rationale: depth_variation is high: log2 library-size IQR 1.86, per-slide medians 636 to 12,194, PC1 tracks depth with |rho| 0.994 on raw counts and still 0.766 after scaling. Library size is spatially structured within tissue, so Moran's I on raw counts would mark depth patterns as spatially variable genes across all ~9,514 detected features. n_features 10000 keeps essentially every feature detected in at least 5% of spots, so the multiple-testing family stays the full set. SVG does not use discovered gro

decisions.rationale: Domains were derived from @batch_correct.embedding, so predicting them from that same embedding is circular. Grouping by patient (8 levels, 1,702 spots each) keeps the independent unit whole. The pathologist 'label' (23% annotated, 6 classes) is used only through label_association, as validation.

Depth differs between slide levels (median library size from 636 to 12,194), so each slide gets its own 3-MAD lower threshold (and at least 2-fold below its median) on log library size and log detected features.
Features detected in fewer than 10 of the 13,417 kept samples carry too little information to normalise or test.

Binomial (Poisson) thinning of counts with the estimated overdispersion would leave a median correlation of 0.049 between the halves of the 9,548 features detected in at least 5% of samples, within 0.05.

decisions.chosen: 2,000 by Pearson residual variance within each slide
decisions.rationale: Residual variances are computed inside each slide level and features variable in the most levels are kept, so features that differ only between levels are not selected as biological variation.
|rho(PC1, log depth)| is 0.52 after log normalisation and 0.49 with Pearson residuals; the difference (+0.04) is not above 0.1, so the simpler log values (interpretable fold changes) are kept.
Expression-type features have very different variances; standardising (clipped at 10 s.d.) lets every feature contribute.
Parallel analysis: 51 leading components have more variance than the 95th percentile of their permutation null (20 permutations of 5000 samples); clamped to the allowed range [5, 50].

Within each patient: silhouette by slide 0.000 and neighbour mixing 0.77 (1 = fully mixed); thresholds: weak at silhouette >= 0.05 or mixing <= 0.8, strong at >= 0.15 or <= 0.5. Differences between patients mix biology and technique and are not counted as batch effect.
13417 samples of raw counts in 36 batches with >= 10 samples each: enough to train a count VAE conditioned on the batch
genes are overdispersed (median var/mean 1.45) but ZINB beats NB by AIC for only 4% of genes (median fitted zero-inflation 0.028); the extra parameter is not supported

decisions.rationale: latent_dim=10 (scVI default; 5 if n<1000); max_epochs=300 (scVI rule min(400, 20000/n x 400), capped by the budget); batch_size=256 (~n/20, power of two in [32, 256]); training capped at 240s.

Set by the plan: every slide belongs to one patient, but batches are corrected across all samples, so differences between patients are removed along with slide effects and structure shared by patients comes forward.
Best batch mixing (0.71 vs 0.32 uncorrected) among candidates keeping >= 50% of within-batch neighbours (0.75).
Each patch covers the spot's own footprint, the tissue its RNA was captured from; it is resized to the encoder's input size.

Highest alignment_recall_at_10 on 500 held-out screening samples, whole groups held out (2 of 8 groups to validation): 0.075 (chance 0.020). Pretrained on: iBOT self-supervision on 40M public pan-cancer histology tiles.

Each sample's features are joined by the mean of its 6 nearest spatial neighbours in the same library (BANKSY), weighted sqrt(1-lambda) : sqrt(lambda); lambda 0.8 favours contiguous domains over cell-type-like clusters.

decisions.decision: spatial domains: method and number of clusters
decisions.rationale: The finest candidate whose every cluster has mean subsample Jaccard >= 0.75 (20 subsamples of 5,000 samples) and whose neighbouring clusters are better separated than one Gaussian group cut in two (largest separation p = 0.050 <= 0.05): kmeans with k=5 (least stable cluster 0.84).
'labels.label' is used only here, after the agent's choices, to measure agreement; it never informed them.

decisions.chosen: 10,000 by Pearson residual variance within each slide
decisions.rationale: Residual variances are computed inside each slide level and features variable in the most levels are kept, so features that differ only between levels are not selected as biological variation.
|rho(PC1, log depth)| is 0.81 after log normalisation and 0.43 with Pearson residuals; residuals remove more depth signal (by 0.38 > 0.1).

Moran's I on the 6-nearest-neighbour graph of each library, centred within library (differences between libraries are not spatial structure), randomisation variance pooled over 36 libraries, Benjamini-Hochberg across features. Calibration: 5.5% of 200 features with permuted positions reach p < 0.05.
Edges between every pair of labels are compared with label permutations that keep each library's label counts; two-sided permutation p-values, Benjamini-Hochberg over 15 pairs.

Samples of one patient are not independent, so whole groups are held out and performance is judged on unseen groups (8 groups). Within each training part the penalty is chosen by grouped inner cross-validation (3 folds, macro-F1).

Samples of one patient are not independent; counts are summed per patient on each side of every contrast and the paired patient-level differences tested (moderated t, BH within each label). The counts are the held-out half of a count split, so the labels were found on other data.
highest mean of trustworthiness and continuity at k=10 (0.819) among maps with seed stability >= 0.5: trustworthiness 0.786, continuity 0.852, stability 1.00.
norm: depth_corr_pc1_after = 0.524296758161773 misses its threshold 0.5; map: trustworthiness@10 = 0.7856759591221311 misses its threshold 0.8

The results answer the objective, so I am not proposing a revision. The five spatial domains are stable (least-stable Jaccard 0.84, k not at the edge of the searched range) and spatially coherent (0.64, against 0.28 for clustering a spot's own features alone). Every domain spans all 8 patients. That made all 5 testable for markers on the held-out half of the counts: 699 markers, all of which keep their sign when any one patient is left out, with 1.35× more found by the naive per-spot test.
